---
title: "The dev server"
---

The server (`crates/server`) is the long-running process behind `preview`: an
[axum](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum) HTTP/websocket server, a
[`notify`](https://github.com/notify-rs/notify) file watcher, and the kernel pool
from [the previous chapter](execution.qmd). There are two of them, `serve.rs`
for a single document and `serve_site.rs` for a directory (site/book), sharing
the small HTTP/asset helpers and the websocket message contract.

## The save → preview loop

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  save["save .qmd"] --> watch["notify watcher<br/>(debounced, filtered)"]
  watch --> kick["wake the rebuild task"]
  kick --> render["re-render + execute cells"]
  render --> diff["diff vs the live block list"]
  diff --> ws["websocket: changed ops"]
  ws --> dom["browser swaps blocks in place"]
```

Saving `post.qmd` drives this loop end to end: the watcher wakes, the rebuild
re-renders and re-runs the changed cell, the diff finds the single changed block,
and the websocket carries one `update` to the browser.

On a websocket connect the server sends a `full_render` (and the page was already
server-rendered into `#qmd-root` for the first paint). On each save it diffs and
broadcasts **only the ops** (`update`/`insert`/`remove`), or a fresh `full_render`
when recovering from a previous failure, plus a `diagnostics` message when those
change. The full message contract is in [the websocket protocol](protocol.qmd).

## Single-document server (`serve.rs`)

`AppState` is the shared state, behind a non-poisoning lock:

```rust
struct AppState {
    doc: parking_lot::Mutex<DocState>,  // title, blocks, diagnostics, …
    tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,      // fan-out of JSON messages to clients
    restart_kernel: AtomicBool,         // set by the dev-menu action
    kick: mpsc::UnboundedSender<()>,    // watcher → rebuild task
}
```

A single spawned task owns the rebuild loop: it waits on `kick`, debounces a
burst of saves (~80 ms), honours a pending kernel restart, then rebuilds. The
rebuild itself (`rebuild`) re-renders the document, runs its cells through the
`Executor`, diffs the new blocks against `DocState.blocks`, and broadcasts the
ops **under the lock** (so a connecting client can't interleave a `full_render`
with an op stream).

### Panic isolation

The rebuild runs in a spawned task, so a panic in the render/exec path would
silently kill hot-reload for the rest of the session. `rebuild_guarded` wraps each
rebuild in `catch_unwind` (via `AssertUnwindSafe` over the awaited future, so the
panic is caught rather than propagated): on a caught panic it pulls a human message
off the payload (`panic_msg` downcasts the `Box<dyn Any>` to `&str`/`String`), logs
it, marks the doc `errored`, and broadcasts a `protocol::error` so every connected
client shows an error overlay. The loop itself survives, so the next good save
re-renders and clears the overlay (the `errored` flag makes that recovery a full
re-mount even when the diff is empty). The **initial render** is guarded the same
way: a document that panics the renderer on first load surfaces the panic as a
connect-time diagnostic instead of crashing startup, so the server still comes up
and can show the error. Because `AppState.doc` is a `parking_lot::Mutex` (not
`std::sync::Mutex`), a panic while the lock is held releases it cleanly rather than
poisoning it, so the next rebuild can take the lock normally.

### The watcher

`spawn_watcher` runs `notify` on its own thread (notify is synchronous; the thread
just parks to stay alive) and forwards qualifying events to the rebuild task through
the same `kick` channel the dev-menu restart uses. It reacts only to
`Modify`/`Create`/`Remove` event kinds, then applies `relevant_path` to each touched
path: the extension must be a known source/asset type, and no path component may be a
generated or VCS directory. The two lists are explicit:

- **extensions:** `qmd`, `md`, `bib`, `csl`, `css`, `scss`, `yml`, `yaml`, `json`,
  `js`, `html`, `svg`, `png`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `gif`;
- **skipped directories:** `_site`, `_book`, `_freeze`, `.git`, `.quarto`,
  `node_modules`.

Skipping `_freeze` matters: the executor writes its own cache there on every run, and
without the skip each write would kick a redundant rebuild. The filter as a whole
keeps an unrelated save (an editor swap file, a build-output write) from triggering a
wasteful 0-op rebuild.

A burst of saves is debounced in the rebuild task, not the watcher: on the first
`kick` it sleeps ~80 ms and then drains any further pending kicks (`try_recv` in a
loop) before doing one rebuild, so a save that touches several files coalesces into a
single re-render. `watch_dirs` watches the document's own directory **plus the
directory of every `{{< include >}}`d file** (recursively, via
`includes::dependencies`), so editing an out-of-tree included partial still refreshes
the preview.

## Multi-page server (`serve_site.rs`)

A directory generalises the single-doc server to a project. State is **per page**,
built lazily on first visit:

```rust
struct SiteApp {
    site: Mutex<Site>,                       // the discovered project (config, pages, …)
    pages: Mutex<HashMap<String, PageState>>, // rel-path → { live blocks, broadcast tx }
    build_tx: UnboundedSender<BuildMsg>,     // → the executor worker
}
```

Navigation between pages is just a real page load (each page has its own
websocket and its own executor), so the navbar / prev-next links work with no SPA.
A save rebuilds only the affected page and hot-reloads it in place with the same
block diff; a `_site.yml` change re-discovers the whole site and reloads open
tabs. A single spawned **executor worker** drains `build_tx`, so each page's cells
run on its own kernel without blocking the HTTP handlers; `build_page_guarded`
gives it the same `catch_unwind` isolation as the single-doc loop. To keep a long
browse from leaking a kernel per visited page, the worker holds at most
`MAX_WARM_PAGES` (6) warm executors and evicts the least-recently-built (dropping its
executor kills its kernel children); an evicted page just pays a cold kernel start on
its next edit.

## Why two servers, not one

The single-doc path has no chrome, no cross-page links, and one block state; the
site path adds per-page state, navigation, listing/chrome expansion, and the
cross-page xref + search index. Keeping them separate keeps each one simple; the
shared surface (the websocket message shapes, the asset/`favicon` helpers, the
embedded client) lives in `serve.rs` and is reused by `serve_site.rs`.

## LAN exposure & the `--host` token

By default the server binds loopback only. `--host` binds `0.0.0.0` so a phone on
the same network can open the live preview (the console prints the LAN URL and a QR
code). That also means anyone on the network could reach it, so a shared guard in
`serve.rs` (`new_session_token` / `lan_access` / `lan_token_guard`, installed via
`with_lan_guard` on both servers) gates **non-loopback** requests behind a
per-session token: the token is a random UUID minted at startup, threaded into the
LAN URL/QR as `?t=…`, and the first tokened load sets a `qmd_token` cookie so the
rest of the session (assets, the websocket upgrade, reloads) authenticates with no
client changes. Loopback peers are detected from `ConnectInfo` and exempted, so the
local workflow (and the editor companion) is unaffected; a non-loopback request with
no/wrong token gets a `403`. The websocket `Origin` check (`origin_allowed`) is an
orthogonal, always-on guard against cross-site driving of the control channel.
